text: New since the system began: automated introduction email, social posting, AI-built public pages, free-text and voice intake, and OAuth account connection. Rules that now apply: (1) EU AI Act Article 50 transparency has applied since 2026-08-02 and was not delayed by the AI Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744); the marking deadline for systems already on the market is 2026-12-02. The outreach message already says it is automated; pages the system builds carried no AI mark, fixed in this change (need ai-output-marking). (2) CAN-SPAM and GDPR/PECR for the intro lane: disclosure, opt-out and a postal address are enforced by outreach/gate.json, which is in dry-run, so nothing has been sent. (3) Still open as owner gates with a default in effect: terms-of-use (no /terms route) and legal-entity (no business/entity.json).

New attack surface since the start: public POST /api/meta/ingest wrote to KV for 12 months with no limit, so anyone could exhaust the daily KV writes; fixed in this change with a per-connection hourly cap and a global daily cap (need meta-signal-write-cap, tested in site/site.test.mjs). None of the four zones sends Strict-Transport-Security (zone setting security_header read through the Cloudflare API 2026-11-20: enabled false on .io, .org, .app, .net); the open item Q-BLINDSPOT-SELF-HSTS carries the fix. Sealed credential tables are left out of the new backup dumps so a copy in R2 cannot leak them. security.txt and SECURITY.md are present; security.txt expires 2027-11-14.

Personal data the system touches that the privacy page did not mention: text sent to AI models (site models on Cloudflare Workers AI via seed/worker/src/airoute.js; the executor uses GitHub Models), microphone failure codes kept 12 months in KV (site/worker.js metaIngest, expirationTtl 31536000; the audio never reaches the site, site/interview.js uses the browser's speech recognition), and the owner session cookie (us_owner, 30 days) with sealed connected accounts (site/passkeys.js). The page now has a card for each, with a test that ties its numbers to the code (need privacy-covers-processing). Visits, ideas and email were already described correctly. The rate-limit counters hold a connection address in a KV key for at most two hours.

Recurring costs and dates the owner had not been shown: all four domains (ultrastable.io, .org, .app, .net) are at Cloudflare Registrar, expire 2027-11-10 and have auto-renew off (Cloudflare Registrar API, read 2026-11-20), so four renewals fall due on one day; the expiry is now re-read weekly and a money gate is filed 60 days out (ops/blindspots/domain-expiry.json, need domain-auto-renew). Platform spend is on free plans: ops/free-tier.json measured 2026-11-17 shows D1 rows read 3.0M of 5M a day, the tightest limit. GitHub Actions stays free for public repositories under the 2026 pricing; private-repository minutes remain a monthly quota guarded by actions-budget.json. No entity and no tax calendar exist (owner gates legal-entity, tax-and-bookkeeping).

If the owner is unreachable for 30 days nothing stops: ticks, lane, deploys and the product manager pass run server-side. What breaks later is what only the owner can pay for or sign in to: the four domains lapse on 2027-11-10 with auto-renew off (need domain-auto-renew), and the Cloudflare and GitHub accounts have no second person (need succession, owner gate). Until today no backup had ever been restored; foundation/backup.py now exports every D1 database and KV namespace weekly, restores each dump into a scratch SQLite database, compares row counts, stores the copy in R2 bucket ultrastable-git and reads it back (need backup-restore stays a gap until the first server-side drill records ok). The domains' zones sit in a different Cloudflare account from the Workers, so losing either account takes the site down.

Changes on platforms the system depends on: (1) Cloudflare D1 has enforced free-plan daily limits since 2026-09-01: once rows read or written pass the limit every query fails until midnight UTC, where overage was tolerated before. Measured use is 60 percent of the read limit (ops/free-tier.json, 2026-11-17) and the free-tier governor samples it (need d1-free-tier-hard-stop). (2) GitHub Actions: hosted-runner prices fell from 2026-01-01, the planned charge for self-hosted runners is postponed with no date, and public repositories remain free. (3) piper-tts moved to GPL-3.0-or-later; it is a CI tool only, recorded in doctrine/dependency-licences.json. doctrine/topology.json listed the R2 bucket ultrastable-git as planned although it has existed since 2026-11-19; corrected in this change.

A web search on 2026-11-20 for ultrastable.io, ultrastable.org and the name with software, platform or startup found nothing published about the system by anyone else: results were Cloudflare's own blog and photonics products that use ultra-stable as a description. So the only public statements are the system's own (site, GitHub organization, MCP registry listing), which CLAIMS-1 checks against code daily. Nothing to correct; the unknown is whether any mention exists outside what a general web search returns, and the sites themselves could not be fetched from this session (network policy), so their live content was not re-read here.
evidence: web search 2026-11-20: "ultrastable.io" OR "ultrastable.org" autonomous system Cloudflare Workers
web search 2026-11-20: "Ultrastable" software OR platform OR startup

text: What a first-minute visitor would not know to ask, checked against the interview: that their words go to AI models and where (now on /privacy, linked from every footer); that a page built for them was written by AI (now labelled on the page); that a one-off idea is refused and why (systemTest in site/worker.js returns not_a_fit with what to use instead); that a running system costs money each month (the front page states setup, commitment and a budget). Not supplied by the interview: what happens to a built page over time. Built pages are kept in KV and the page says nothing about how long; registered as a question for the next sweep, not as a claim.

Rules and signals for automated mail: Gmail, Yahoo and Microsoft require SPF, DKIM and DMARC alignment and expect one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058) on automated mail. DNS read through the Cloudflare API on 2026-11-20: the sending subdomain outreach.ultrastable.org has DKIM, SPF and DMARC p=reject; the apex domains ultrastable.io and ultrastable.org have SPF and DKIM but no DMARC record (the open item Q-BLINDSPOT-SELF-DMARC carries the fix); ultrastable.app and .net publish no mail records. The intro message has an opt-out line and domain-wide suppression (4 lines in outreach/suppression.json) but no List-Unsubscribe header (need one-click-unsubscribe, to land before the gate leaves dry-run). outreach/gate.json is in dry-run with kill false, so every send so far was simulated.

Pages and flows added or changed in this sweep: three new cards on /privacy, a 'Written by AI' label on built pages, ; earlier pages are covered by the UI audit's own baseline. The UI/UX loop's last record (ops/uiux/status.json, 2026-11-19) covers 22 pages with 0 blocking findings and every user path passing, in offline mode; its analytics read failed with HTTP 403, so funnels are unmeasured. The new label uses 14px text, dark on white, inside the existing fixed bar, within the design contract. Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour of built pages is not audited by any loop, because their HTML is written per idea; that is the open unknown for the next sweep.

Name: two US registrations of ULTRASTABLE exist and both are dead (serial 74237462, class 1 photographic film, cancelled 2004-03-13; serial 75744220, class 17 laminate substrates, abandoned 2001); no live mark in software classes 9 or 42 and no software company trading under the name surfaced. EUIPO, WIPO and UKIPO were not searched (need name-clearance-eu-wipo). The word is also a descriptive cybernetics term, so it is weak as an exclusive mark for anyone. Licence and dependencies: the runtime code has no third-party dependency; 11 build and CI tools are inventoried with licences, all allowed for tool use (psycopg LGPL-3.0, piper-tts GPL-3.0-or-later and axe-core MPL-2.0 are tools only, never shipped), and a test now fails on a new dependency without an allowed licence.
